neighbours.label: The stand-in verb or repeated verb in the second arm of a comparison or analogy (like the retail sector ⟦did⟧, would be like ⟦asking⟧ a fish…, than there ⟦is⟧ for…, just as they ⟦had⟧), and the word right after it
fire: Electric cars today feel a lot like mobile phones did around the year 2000.
Expecting him to apologise would be like expecting a cat to fetch the paper.
There is no more evidence for this theory than there was for the last one.
She handled the crisis calmly, just as her mother had during the strike.
Banning the book now would be like banning the printing press back then.
Online classes are spreading the way correspondence courses did a century ago.
He treats his garden the same way a chess player does an opening.
The new mayor governs much as the old one did in his first term.
quiet: Electric cars today feel a lot faster and quieter around the city.
Expecting him to apologise, she waited by the door with the paper.
There is no evidence for this theory, and there was none last year.
She handled the crisis calmly, and her mother was proud during the strike.
Banning the book now would anger the printers and the readers.
Online classes are spreading, and correspondence courses ended a century ago.
He treats his garden well and plays chess in the evening.
The new mayor governs carefully, and the old one retired after his first term.

short: pro-verb in a comparison's second arm
notes: Card: peaks on ' in', ' of', ' as', ' for' just after the second arm of 'like X did', 'the same … as', 'than there is'. Probes peaked on the pro-verb itself: like … did 0.61, like asking 0.66, than there is 0.47, as they had 0.27; the same content without a comparison 0.01-0.02.
